common_hypotheses.spaces: H and K are nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. Qudit supplies the normed additive group, complex inner product, completeness and finite dimensionality; Nontrivial excludes dimension zero.
common_hypotheses.channels: N and M are CPTP maps L(H) -> L(K): complex-linear, positive under every finite matrix amplification, and trace-preserving for every operator. Input and output dimensions need not agree.

definitions.mathematics: A positive semidefinite operator rho with Tr(rho)=1; invertibility is not required.
ker(sigma) is a subspace of ker(rho); for the positive states at issue this is supp(rho) subset supp(sigma).
sandwichedQuasi returns the complex trace Tr[(sigma^((1-alpha)/(2 alpha)) rho sigma^((1-alpha)/(2 alpha)))^alpha]. This report denotes its real part by Q_alpha(rho,sigma). All powers use CFC.rpow.
Multiply an extended-real value by 1/ln(2). All divergence formulas in this report use base-2 logarithms (bits).

For normalized states and alpha >= 1/2, alpha != 1: +infinity if alpha>1 and supp(rho) is not contained in supp(sigma); +infinity if alpha<1 and Q_alpha=0; otherwise log_2(Q_alpha)/(alpha-1). The actual total definition is toBits(sandwichedRenyiDivNN alpha rho.op sigma.op); the lower-order infinity test also requires rho!=0, automatic for normalized states.
If supp(rho) subset supp(sigma), Re Tr[rho (CFC.log rho - CFC.log sigma)]/ln(2); otherwise +infinity. Trace normalization removes the dependency expression division by Re Tr(rho).
A unit vector psi in the specified complex Hilbert space; PureInput.density is |psi><psi|.
For E:L(H)->L(K), apply E tensor id_H to a state on H tensor H, yielding a state on K tensor H.
Supremum over all unit vectors psi in H tensor H of stateRenyi alpha ((N tensor id_H)(|psi><psi|)) ((M tensor id_H)(|psi><psi|)), after EReal.toENNReal conversion.
Same pure-state, same-reference-space supremum as channelRenyi, using stateRelative and then EReal.toENNReal conversion.
H_0 is EuclideanSpace C (Fin 1); H_(n+1)=H tensor H_n. Thus H_n is H^tensor n with a terminal one-dimensional tensor factor and specified association.
N_0 is the identity on the one-dimensional tensor unit and N_(n+1)=N tensor N_n, hence N^tensor n under ordinary tensor-unit identifications.
B_alpha(n)=channelRenyi alpha N_n M_n. Pure inputs are on H_n tensor H_n, reference dimension is (dim H)^n, and output states lie on K_n tensor H_n.
B(n)=channelRelative N_n M_n, with the same input, reference and output spaces as blockRenyi.
R_alpha = sup over positive natural numbers n of B_alpha(n)/n in [0,+infinity]. It is defined as a supremum, not as a limit.
R = sup over positive natural numbers n of B(n)/n in [0,+infinity]. It is defined as a supremum, not as a limit.
A dependent pair (n,psi) with n a positive natural number and psi a unit vector on H_n tensor H_n.
The stateRenyi divergence of the two n-block amplified outputs at the selected pure input, converted to ENNReal and divided by n.
The stateRelative divergence of the two n-block amplified outputs at the selected pure input, converted to ENNReal and divided by n.

conventions.state_value_type: EReal, the extended reals. The explicit definitions at issue return finite real values or +infinity.
conventions.channel_block_regularized_value_type: ENNReal (Lean notation ℝ≥0∞), the extended nonnegative reals [0,+infinity], with their usual order topology.
conventions.toENNReal: Preserves +infinity; a finite real x maps to max(x,0), and -infinity maps to zero. Source nonnegativity propositions show clipping is harmless for alpha>=1/2, alpha!=1 and for stateRelative.
conventions.spectral_powers: CFC.rpow uses the scalar zero-eigenvalue conventions 0^t=0 for t!=0 and 0^0=1, including negative exponents. Thus inverse powers vanish on the kernel.
conventions.spectral_logarithm: CFC.log uses Real.log; Real.log(0)=0. Infinity is handled by the explicit support/quasi-entropy tests.
conventions.order_one_totalization: At alpha=1, both strict-order infinity tests are false and 1/(alpha-1)=0 in Lean real division. Consequently stateRenyi 1 and regularizedRenyi 1 are zero. The limit theorem excludes that assigned value. This is a definition-level observation, not a separately checked Lean theorem in this review.
conventions.zero_block: Regularized suprema explicitly exclude n=0; the sequence expressions have a totalized n=0 term, immaterial to convergence at natural-number atTop.
conventions.infinite_limit: A limit equal to +infinity means eventual exceedance of every finite bound.

declarations.formal_statement: Tendsto (fun α => regularizedRenyi α N M) (𝓝[≠] (1 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (regularizedRelative N M))
declarations.mathematical_description: For every pair of CPTP maps N,M on nonzero finite-dimensional complex input and output Hilbert spaces, lim_(alpha->1, alpha!=1) sup_(n>=1) [channelRenyi alpha N^tensor n M^tensor n]/n = sup_(n>=1) [channelRelative N^tensor n M^tensor n]/n in [0,+infinity].
declarations.source_filter: Punctured two-sided real neighborhood filter at 1 (𝓝[≠] 1).
declarations.target_filter: Neighborhood filter of regularizedRelative N M in ENNReal.
declarations.order_domain_note: No explicit restriction on real alpha in the source filter; all alpha sufficiently close to 1 are greater than 1/2.

declarations.formal_statement: Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => blockRenyi p N M n / (n : ℝ≥0∞)) atTop (𝓝 (regularizedRenyi p N M))
declarations.mathematical_description: For every such pair N,M and every fixed real p>=1/2, p!=1, lim_(n->infinity) [channelRenyi p N^tensor n M^tensor n]/n = sup_(n>=1) [channelRenyi p N^tensor n M^tensor n]/n in [0,+infinity].
declarations.target_filter: Neighborhood filter of regularizedRenyi p N M in ENNReal.

declarations.formal_statement: Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => blockRelative N M n / (n : ℝ≥0∞)) atTop (𝓝 (regularizedRelative N M))
declarations.mathematical_description: For every such pair N,M, lim_(n->infinity) [channelRelative N^tensor n M^tensor n]/n = sup_(n>=1) [channelRelative N^tensor n M^tensor n]/n in [0,+infinity].
declarations.target_filter: Neighborhood filter of regularizedRelative N M in ENNReal.

subtleties_for_later_human_comparison: The stabilized input definition literally quantifies over pure vectors with a reference equal to the input space; an arbitrary-ancilla or mixed-state presentation requires a separate equivalence argument.
Tensor powers carry an explicit terminal one-dimensional factor; compare with standard tensor powers using the usual unit identifications.
Regularization is a supremum over positive lengths; block convergence is supplied by the latter two theorem statements.
Order-one convergence is punctured and two-sided, rather than continuity of the assigned value at alpha=1.
Support failure above order 1 and zero quasi-entropy below order 1 are distinct infinity conventions.
No declaration asserts a rate, uniformity in channels/order, or a general interchange of the order and block limits.
